headline: Steering biological sequence generators toward target criteria via diverse conditioning
label: Target Conditioned Molecular Design
summary: Recent preprints from late January 2026 pair generative sequence models with RL, Schrödinger bridges, and language-model priors for target-specific design.
synthesis: The dominant thread is steering a generative model for biological sequences toward a specified target criterion rather than sampling unconditionally. SOLD couples a latent diffusion model with RNA-FM embeddings and reinforcement learning to optimize secondary structure, minimum free energy, and LDDT for RNA inverse folding. MadSBM formulates peptide sequence design as a rate-based discrete Schrödinger bridge, using protein language model priors and functional guidance. ProDCARL aligns an EvoDiff diffusion peptide generator with RL rewards from AMP activity and toxicity predictors. The fourth preprint, on repetition in ESM-3 and ProtGPT2, applies a related steering approach, utility-controlled contrastive steering (UCCS), to protein language models. What is new is less a shared input modality than the range of conditioning inputs and the mechanisms used to inject them: latent embeddings, language-model priors, and reward signals.
